title: JSON guardrails: mutation-based constrained-decoder & streaming-recovery chaos tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Validate JSON-mode enforcement and the constrained-decoder behavior across streaming responses, function/tool-calling flows, and compatibility/legacy model variants. This ticket implements a mutation-driven chaos harness to exercise edge cases: truncated streams, interleaved tool-calls, schema evolution (added/removed fields), and decoder recovery heuristics. Goals: 1) catch regressions introduced by kernel scheduling and batching that produce malformed partial JSON in stream-mode; 2) verify constrained-decoder enforces field types and required keys when strict mode is enabled; 3) ensure compat layer fallbacks (permissive decoder, auto-correction heuristics) do not produce silent data loss for downstream tools.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job ci/structured-output-e2e passes on runtime-1.20 with <0.5% strict-mode schema violations across the matrix of models and sequence lengths. 2) Streaming partial-recovery heuristics validated: at least 95% of truncated-chunk cases repaired by 'KV-prefix reassembly' produce valid JSON or explicit decoder error tokens. 3) Tool-calling sequences that include nested JSON arguments never cause silent field drops in permissive mode; violations must surface as structured error objects. 4) Compatibility matrix documented: for each model family and runtime variant, expected decoder mode (strict|permissive) and recommended fallback policy are recorded.
test_plan: 1) Corpus: golden_json_contracts_v3 (200 prompts) + synthetic mutations. 2) Mutation strategies: byte-flip, chunk-drop, field-type-swaps, extra-commas, duplicated-keys, name-mangling, array-truncation. 3) Harness: json-guard-chaos (Go harness in infra/testbeds) runs 10k mutations per model/variant. 4) Streaming scenarios: reorder-chunks, delayed-chunk, truncated-tail, chunk-merge; measure decoder outputs and error codes. 5) Tool-calling scenarios: insert '__tool_call__' tokens, nested JSON arguments, function-return streaming; assert schema for both tool payload and final message. 6) Metrics: schema_violation_rate, recovery_rate, false_positive_rate (decoder flags invalid but downstream tolerant), mean_time_to_detect (ms). 7) CI: schedule nightly runs plus pre-merge smoke for PRs touching decoder/streaming/compat layers.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created; spec reviewed with Applied ML and Console teams. Identified golden prompt set and initial mutation strategies.

2026-03-12: Initial harness prototype (json-guard-chaos) implemented; can replay streaming chunks and inject truncations. First run against model-x-small completed — observed 1.9% schema violations in strict mode (expected baseline).
2026-03-13: Added tool-calling sequence generator and nested-arg templates. Discovered several cases where permissive decoder silently dropped optional numeric fields during batching-heavy workloads.
2026-03-14: Tuned KV-prefix reassembly heuristic and reduced repair false-positives. Running full matrix on dedicated test cluster; exporting results to dashboard.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): Prefer default strict-mode for new customers; enable permissive as opt-in with clear telemetry. Add release notes guidance.
Design (Maya Chen): UX needs explicit error object formatting so Console can show parsing issues without raw logs.
Infra (Ravi Kapoor): Suggest running heavy mutation jobs on Dedicated CI pool to avoid flapping cloud quotas; add resource tags.
notes: Decision notes: We choose a two-tier approach — strict enforcement at API boundary for paid tiers and permissive+telemetry for legacy/compatibility where customers have opted in. Recovery heuristics are intentionally conservative: prefer explicit decoder error objects over automatic field inference when ambiguity exceeds threshold. Follow-ups: create PM ticket for customer communication & SDK change to expose structured parse errors; add e2e test to simulate on-prem private deployment network flakiness.
